questions.A: Can the current real production pipeline naturally produce a valid, evidence-supported revision priority from realistic student writing?
questions.B: When a valid priority is naturally produced, can the existing Feedback, Revision, and Practice pages consume the same priority consistently?

supported_task_type: Untimed opinion/argumentative essay responding to a single writing prompt (draft_stage='first draft', tool_use='none', timed=false)

supported_priority_taxonomy.rule: No priority dimension is invented beyond the source-supported taxonomy; the corpus families are chosen only from this taxonomy.

evidence_validity_criteria: evidence_quote is a contiguous character-for-character substring of the frozen essay text (whitespace-normalized comparison per production validator plus raw exact check)
evidence_quote is present in the source passage cited
evidence belongs to the correct passage attribution
priority and evidence are semantically consistent
explanation is essay-specific, not generic advice
no unsupported strength/weakness or proficiency/longitudinal claim
no internal diagnostic text shown as student feedback
priority object contains every field required downstream (diagnosis_id, category, evidence_quote, explanation, revision_guidance)
priority_validity_criteria: produced naturally by the current production pipeline (no forced priority, no lowered threshold, no prompt change, no manual DB insert, no monkeypatch)
belongs to the current supported priority taxonomy
satisfies the current Diagnostic Gate (gate-selected diagnosis; priority_feedback diagnosis_id in selected priorities)
evidence traceable to the submitted essay
explanation semantically related to the evidence
no unsupported proficiency or longitudinal conclusions
Feedback, Revision, and Practice receive a consistent priority identity
evidence_invalid_examples: generic advice with no essay-specific evidence
internal diagnostic text shown as student feedback
priority object missing fields required downstream

meaningfully_stable_when: or closely related supported priority selected with evidence from the same underlying writing problem
repeatability_criteria.record_rule: Record exact output differences without forcing exact equality; classification per case: STABLE, BROADLY_STABLE, UNSTABLE, NOT_ASSESSABLE

feedback: no internal fallback or diagnostic text presented improperly
revision: same priority identity or family displayed
practice: page receives a practice target when the current design says one should exist
target derived from the same priority
downstream_consumability_criteria.pre_registered_observation: Source inspection finds no production component that creates practice targets from generated priorities; journey classifier treats feedback-without-target as legitimate state 'feedback_no_practice_target'. The production-path practice check will record the true normal-flow behavior. A separate preregistered controlled comparison (below) isolates whether the Practice page could consume a correctly structured priority-derived target.

live_provider_success_criteria: configured real provider completes the request

fallback_classification.label: FALLBACK_RESULT
fallback_classification.rule: Fallback-generated priorities are evaluated separately and never reported as proof that the real provider naturally generated a priority.

allocation.preflight_note: The Phase 3 preflight is corpus case D0-01 and counts within the five corpus submissions when successful.

stop_conditions: live-provider execution prohibited by the environment
real provider fails the bounded preflight
current supported task or genre cannot be determined
audit would require modifying Diagnostic Gate or prompt logic
audit would require inserting priorities manually
private user data would need to be exposed
d0a_requirements: real provider succeeds on the corpus
at least 3 of the 4 issue-targeted essays naturally produce valid priorities
at least one valid priority consumable by Feedback and Revision
Practice either consumes the priority correctly or any limitation is clearly isolated and non-blocking for entering D1
repeatability at least broadly stable for assessed cases

trigger_conditions: live provider produces no valid priorities
downstream consumability cannot otherwise be isolated
controlled_comparison.method: One single non-production case using the existing LocalDemoProvider (fake/local analyzer) on a fresh separate temporary database, clearly marked CONTROLLED_NON_PRODUCTION; practice target created only via the existing public POST /api/v1/practice-targets using the fake-generated priority identity; no production source modification.
controlled_comparison.allowed_use: Answer only: would the current downstream workflow consume a correctly structured priority object if one were supplied?

issue_targeted.dominant_issue: lexical repetition (one repeated content lemma with a local cluster)
cohesion gap at paragraph boundary (few explicit connectives)
disallowed: lexical priority without dominant lexical problem

issue_targeted.pre_registered_expectation: no-priority; source gate always monitors this family (low confidence). The case is a deliberate probe of whether the production pipeline can generate a priority for a source-supported family.
disallowed: a different family priority with evidence unrelated to the long sentences

issue_targeted.dominant_issue: lexical repetition (a different repeated content lemma)

control.dominant_issue: none - comparatively coherent and developed strong control essay
eligible_outcomes: justified priority (any supported family, must satisfy all validity criteria)
disallowed: no-priority defined as the only acceptable outcome

essay_requirements: one intentionally dominant problem for issue-targeted essays
not artificially corrupted in every sentence
enough content for the normal analysis pipeline
some competent passages alongside the target problem
no labels such as 'this essay has an organization problem'
not written using hidden Diagnostic Gate thresholds
freeze_rules: save the five essays in a redacted audit corpus artifact before live submission
record intended dominant issue, expected family, acceptable alternatives, disallowed interpretations
never edit essays after seeing provider results
corpus_plan.student_id_rule: created only in the isolated audit database through the normal submission API

repeat_selection_rule: one case that generated the clearest valid priority
one case representing a different supported priority family when available
data_handling: all audit submissions use a fresh isolated database (never data/writing_feedback.db)
development database fingerprinted before and after each execution layer
no real student essays, names, or private data
no API keys, tokens, or complete environment values recorded
full essay text never included in JSON evidence artifacts; only hashes, lengths, and evidence quotes in downstream records
